title: Collection cannot load because index_null_offset is missing after upgrading Milvus
body: I created a collection in Milvus 2.5.0 with 500 partitions, an IVF_FLAT COSINE index on a 1024-dimensional image_vector field, and an image_desc VARCHAR field configured with enable_analyzer=True and enable_match=True. After about a month, loading a partition began failing with an invalid local path for index_null_offset, which made vector search unavailable. I am now using Milvus 2.5.4 in standalone mode on CentOS with Kafka and pymilvus 2.5.4. Moving the 2.5.0 data into the 2.5.4 directory did not resolve it, and deleting and recreating the vector index did not help.

symptoms_visible: The collection's partitions cannot load because Milvus reports an invalid local path ending in index_null_offset, so vector search is unavailable.
The same load error remains after moving the old data to the 2.5.4 directory and after deleting and recreating the IVF_FLAT vector index.
N0.label: N0 missing index_null_offset reported

symptoms_visible: Releasing and loading the collection again still gets stuck with the missing index_null_offset path.
The collection has a text-match field and a separate IVF_FLAT vector field.
N1.label: N1 logs and schema details collected

symptoms_visible: The collection still cannot load because index_null_offset is absent.
N2.label: N2 etcd backup available

symptoms_visible: I ran collection.compact(), but no index rebuild was triggered and the collection remains unavailable.
N2_x.label: N2_x old-version compaction aftermath

symptoms_visible: After upgrading to the fixed version and running manual or Birdwatcher compaction, some segments changed but the collection still cannot load because index_null_offset files are missing.
N3_x.label: N3_x fixed-version compaction incomplete

symptoms_visible: The compaction list contains completed or cleaned tasks, but the same large flushed segments remain and the collection still cannot load.
The segments that never get rewritten are larger than the configured 2 GiB segment maxSize.
N4.label: N4 oversized uncompacted segments identified

symptoms_visible: After increasing segment maxSize from 2 GiB to 3 GiB and manually triggering compaction, the collection loads successfully.
N_terminal.label: terminal collection loaded

question_patterns: Can you export and attach the complete Milvus logs covering the load failure?
Please release and reload the collection, then attach the Kubernetes pod logs from that attempt.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I exported the Kubernetes pod logs with export-milvus-log.sh and uploaded them. I also uploaded a second log covering only release collection and load collection.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The reload log has no missing index file error; it shows the collection loading successfully and only the client timing out.
I exported the same failure logs with kubectl instead of export-milvus-log.sh.

question_patterns: Do you have any indexes or indexed fields other than the vector field and text-match field?
Can you list all fields in the collection and their index-related settings?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I only have four fields: image_id as the VARCHAR primary key, image_vector as a 1024-dimensional FLOAT_VECTOR, image_desc as a VARCHAR with the Chinese analyzer and enable_match=True, and another plain VARCHAR field named index. IVF_FLAT is configured only on image_vector.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: There is no field with enable_match=True; the collection only has the primary key and vector index.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c1, c8, c12, c19: the opening reporter uploaded Kubernetes logs, confirmed release/reload remained stuck, and restated the four-field schema. The image in c3 was produced by a maintainer, not by the reporter, so it is not attached to a user answer.

question_patterns: Can you use Birdwatcher to create an etcd backup and attach the backup file?
Please collect the instance metadata with Birdwatcher so we can inspect the affected index records.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I used the precompiled Birdwatcher binary and uploaded bw_etcd_ALL.250217-064143.bak.gz.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I cannot obtain the etcd backup, and the logs do not contain the affected collection or index metadata.
I created the same full etcd backup with a different Birdwatcher build.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c17-c23: the reporter initially had trouble building Birdwatcher, then used the supplied release binary and uploaded the backup. The installation-error screenshot from c21 is logistical and is omitted under the denoise rule.

solution.intent: Issue collection.compact() on the existing deployment to regenerate the missing index file.
solution.concrete_example: Run collection.compact() for the affected collection and then retry loading it.
solution.inference_hint: Inspection of the uploaded etcd backup established that index_null_offset belongs to the text-match index, used the wrong storage prefix, and was garbage-collected unintentionally. That diagnosis was supplied by the maintainer in c24, not by the reporter.

edges.comment: Reporter and maintainer messages c24-c27: compaction was suggested as recovery, but the opening reporter ran collection.compact() and reported that no index rebuild was triggered.

solution.intent: Upgrade to Milvus 2.5.5, which contains the storage-prefix fix, then issue manual compaction to regenerate index files for historical segments before loading the collection.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade to Milvus 2.5.5, run client.compact(collection_name), wait for all compaction tasks to finish, and then reload the collection.
solution.inference_hint: The backup showed that the missing file was generated for image_desc's text-match index, not for image_vector's IVF_FLAT index. The product fix prevents the wrong-prefix garbage collection, while compaction is needed to rewrite already affected data.

edges.comment: Messages c28-c38 and c34-c39: the maintainers stated that the prefix bug was fixed in 2.5.5 and prescribed manual compaction for existing data. A second affected operator upgraded and compacted, but some old segments remained and the collection still failed to load. This second operator is explicitly folded into the simulated user side because the opening reporter did not later report a production retest.

solution.intent: Skip ineffective compaction on the old deployment: upgrade to the build containing the storage-prefix fix, then manually compact the existing collection and reload it.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade to Milvus 2.5.5 first, run client.compact(collection_name), wait for the tasks to complete, and retry loading the collection.
solution.inference_hint: The wrong-prefix garbage collection diagnosis comes from maintainer inspection of the backup. Upgrading prevents recurrence, but recovery of old segments still depends on successful compaction.

edges.comment: Shortcut counterpart to e4: it allows an agent to recommend the fixed build and recovery compaction without first repeating the already falsified old-version collection.compact() attempt. The destination includes the later second-operator observation that ordinary compaction remained incomplete.

question_patterns: Can you share the compaction task output and the current segment inventory for the affected collection?
Which segments remain after compaction, and what states and sizes do they have?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran force compaction through Birdwatcher and pasted the show compactions output and segment information. Several tasks say completed or cleaned, but the same flushed segments remain and loading still reports missing index files.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every old segment was replaced by a new segment after compaction, but the new segments still reference missing index_null_offset files.
The task IDs differ, but the output still shows that the same flushed segments survive repeated compactions.

question_patterns: Can you compare the size of the segments that remain with the configured segment maxSize?
Are the segments skipped by repeated compaction larger than the current segment size limit?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I checked the memory sizes of all flushed segments. The segments that never got compacted are larger than the configured segment maxSize of 2 GiB; the smaller ones were recreated and dropped during compaction.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: All remaining segments are well below 2 GiB, and raising segment maxSize does not change which segments are compacted.

edges.comment: Second affected operator messages c36-c41, folded into the user side: the operator pasted raw Birdwatcher compaction output, segment inventory, and their size comparison. The later successful configuration change is not leaked into these questions.

solution.intent: On the fixed Milvus version, temporarily raise segment maxSize enough to make the surviving oversized segments eligible for rewriting, manually trigger compaction, wait for it to finish, and verify that the collection loads.
solution.concrete_example: Change segment maxSize from 2 GiB to 3 GiB, manually trigger collection compaction again, wait for the task to complete, and retry loading the collection.
solution.inference_hint: The primary defect is the text-match index_null_offset file being garbage-collected because its path used the wrong prefix. The remaining recovery obstacle is that the affected oversized segments were not rewritten under the 2 GiB maxSize; increasing the limit enabled the subsequent manual compaction to replace them.

edges.comment: Second affected operator messages c42-c44: after raising segment maxSize from 2 GiB to 3 GiB and still manually triggering compaction, the operator confirmed that the collection loaded successfully. Maintainers acknowledged the abnormal compaction behavior and tracked its separate fix in c45-c47.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted primary root cause: index_null_offset belongs to the enable_match text index on image_desc, and its wrong storage prefix caused it to be garbage-collected unintentionally; it is separate from the IVF_FLAT index on image_vector.
Diagnosis must be grounded in the uploaded logs, collection schema, and Birdwatcher etcd backup rather than inferred from the missing filename alone.
Must not recommend recreating the IVF_FLAT vector index, moving the old data directory, or merely releasing and reloading the collection as the fix, because those actions were already ineffective.
Recovery must use a Milvus build containing the prefix fix and regenerate files for historical data through completed manual compaction.

If ordinary or forced compaction leaves oversized old segments unchanged, must account for the observed 2 GiB maxSize barrier by raising segment maxSize sufficiently and manually triggering compaction again.
Must ask the affected user to verify that compaction completed and the collection loads successfully before declaring resolution.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Milvus operator who can manage Kubernetes logs, inspect collection schemas and storage paths, run Birdwatcher, perform upgrades and compaction, and compare segment metadata. A second affected production operator contributes the final compaction investigation and successful recovery and is explicitly folded into the user side.
persona_hint.communication_style: Urgent, direct, and cooperative; supplies logs and backups when requested, asks practical recovery questions, and reports exact commands and observable outcomes.
